### Morningstar Announces Agenda for Morningstar Sustainable Investing Summit 2027


September 10, 2026


*Global leaders to gather in Amsterdam to explore climate commitments and real-world action, amongst other crucial topics for institutional investors and asset owners.*


AMSTERDAM, 10 September 2026 – Morningstar Europe Limited, a subsidiary of Morningstar, Inc. (NASDAQ: MORN) and leading provider of independent investment insights, has announced the agenda for the Morningstar Sustainable Investing Summit to be held on 2-3 February 2027 at Beurs van Berlage, Amsterdam.


Set against the theme "Focus on What Matters", this year's summit will examine whether sustainable investing can move from commitment to proof. Institutional investors face a widening gap between the climate ambitions they've set and the real-world outcomes they can actually deliver. Right now, asset owners are being asked to close that gap.


That test runs through every part of the agenda. On regulation, the summit asks what happens when the compliance frameworks asset owners have built entire programmes around are tested by changing political priorities and regulation. On accountability, it will explore whether stewardship and voting are driving genuine change, or whether they risk simply generating paperwork and political backlash. On private markets, it confronts an important question: with private capital having passed 14.5 trillion dollars and heading toward 20 trillion, is there a consistent answer to what sustainable investing means outside the public markets?


The event will gather institutional investors, global thought leaders, and academics for two days of data-driven insight and discussion. Sessions will explore business ethics, nature and physical climate risk, sustainable investing in private markets, stewardship and voting, regulatory change, the demands of AI, and the transition to a more sustainable economy.


*“Sustainable investing continues to be tested by market, political, and technological change with AI. This summit brings together the research and practitioner insights that asset owners and institutional investors need to focus on material risks, identify opportunities and make better long-term investment decisions,”* said **Kunal Kapoor, Chief Executive Officer of Morningstar.**


Speakers include:


- Alison Taylor, Clinical Associate Professor, NYU Stern School of Business;
- Barbara Lambotte, Head of Research, Morningstar Sustainalytics;
- Fabiana Fedeli, CIO Equities, Multi Asset and Sustainability, M&G Investments;
- Kunal Kapoor, CEO, Morningstar;
- Lindsey Stewart, Director of Institutional Insights, Morningstar;
- Marc Palahi, Chief Nature Officer, Lombard Odier;
- Monika Calay, Director of UK Manager Research, Morningstar;
- Maria Nazarova-Doyle, Global Head of Sustainable Investment, IFM;
- Catalina Secreteanu, Global Head of Market Development, Morningstar Sustainalytics;
- Anikka Villegas, Senior Research Analyst, Fund Strategies & Sustainable Investing, PitchBook, a Morningstar company.


Key sessions include:


**Higher Ground and the Changing Landscape for Business Ethics:** Alison Taylor will examine why ethical business has become more difficult, the tensions between legal and ethical frameworks, and why human rights have a key role in finding a way forward.


**Signals on Sustainability: What’s the Market Telling Us Now?** Lindsey Stewart will use Morningstar and wider market research to assess what stewardship disclosures and proxy voting reveal about changing investor priorities.


**ESG From 35 Years Ago to Now – How Screening and Risk Management Have Evolved:** Barbara Lambotte will trace the development of sustainability analysis, from values-based screening to more sophisticated assessments of materiality and investment risk.


**The Chief Investment Officer Panel – Sustainable Investing in a Fractured World:** Moderated by Monika Calay, investment leaders from M&G, IFM and Morgan Stanley Investment Management will discuss the energy demands of the AI boom, the outlook for the energy transition and the place of defence in sustainable portfolios.


**Climate Investing in the Private Capital Ecosystem:** Anikka Villegas will examine how economic, geopolitical and technological change is reshaping climate investing across venture capital, private equity and infrastructure, and where private markets can help support the transition to a more sustainable economy.


**From Commitment to Impact – Real-World Climate Action at Leading European Pension Funds:** Moderated by Catalina Secreteanu, senior investment leaders will consider where capital is most needed, how stewardship and engagement can support change, and what it will take to mobilise investment into the economy.


The full agenda, speaker biographies, and further information are available[here](https://www.morningstar.com/business/events/morningstar-sustainable-investing-summit/agenda?refid=agendapressrelease) .

**About Morningstar, Inc.**
Morningstar, Inc. is a leading provider of independent investment insights in North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia. The Company offers an extensive line of products and solutions that serve a wide range of market participants, including individual and institutional investors in public and private capital markets, financial advisors and wealth managers, asset managers, retirement plan providers and sponsors, and issuers of fixed-income securities. Morningstar provides data and research insights on a wide range of investment offerings, including managed investment products, publicly listed companies, private capital markets, debt securities, and real-time global market data. Morningstar also offers investment management services through its investment advisory subsidiaries, with approximately $375 billion in AUMA as of June 30, 2026. The Company operates through wholly-owned subsidiaries in 32 countries. For more information, visit www.morningstar.com/company. Follow Morningstar on LinkedIn @Morningstar.
